title: Residents' and assessors' experience of entrustable professional activity assessment burden in an internal medicine residency
subtitle: Qualitative interview and focus-group study before the June review of assessment targets
statement: Residents in a 64-resident internal medicine programme must collect at least 12 workplace-based assessments of entrustable professional activities per four-week rotation. Last year 38 percent of assessments were completed more than seven days after the observed activity and the median narrative comment was nine words long. The programme does not know how residents and assessors experience this workload, which parts of it matter to them, or what they believe the assessments are for, and the competency committee will revise the targets in June without that knowledge.
whoAffected: Residents in all three training years, the faculty who observe and rate them, chief residents who sit between the two, and the programme administrators who monitor completion.
whatHurts: Late and thin assessments give the competency committee weak evidence for progression decisions, residents spend time chasing signatures and may avoid difficult encounters, and assessors complete forms from memory in batches.
currentPractice: A minimum of 12 app-based assessments per rotation, each with an entrustment rating and a free-text comment; completion rates are reported to the programme evaluation committee each month.
whyNow: The competency committee revises assessment targets next June, and the app export shows a pattern of delay that numbers alone cannot explain.
constraints: No external funding. The research assistant is funded at 0.2 FTE until June 2027. Interviews must fit around clinical duties (lunch hours or the protected academic half-day). Individual residents' assessment records may not be viewed without their written consent.
patientCenteredGoal: Assessment that helps residents become safe, independent physicians, so that patients are cared for by doctors whose readiness was judged on real observation rather than on forms completed to reach a quota.
summary: Problem framed as a qualitative question about how assessment workload is experienced and why assessments are late, thin or strategically chosen.
